evidence: Cic. Cat. 3.25: ut omnēs salvī cōnservārēminī (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 61: nōn salva vidēris, you don’t look well
Traupman 184: tē salvum et sānum domum rediisse, that you came home safe and sound
terms.comment: Saved, unharmed, well: the word behind the greetings salvē and salvus sīs, and Satin' salvē?, is everything all right? Often paired: salvus atque incolumis (Caes. B.C. 2.32).

evidence: Caes. B.G. 6.40.4: incolumēs ad ūnum omnēs in castra perveniunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Unhurt and whole, of people, armies, ships, cities; the ablative is incolumī.

phrases.latin: vīsam tē incolumem audiamque Hibērum narrantem loca, facta, nātiōnēs, ut mōs est tuus
phrases.english: I’ll see you safe and sound and hear you tell of the places, deeds and peoples of Spain, as you always do

phrases.latin: incolumēs ad ūnum omnēs in castra perveniunt
phrases.english: they all reach the camp safe, to a man
